newsitem.title: USA: Trusted Information says has encryption approval.
newsitem.headline: Trusted Information says has encryption approval.

text.p: Trusted Information Systems Inc was one of the first three companies to win permission from U.S. Commerce Department to export a 56-bit encryption product, a company official said Friday.
Earlier on Friday, Commerce Department said it had granted the first three approvals under a new Clinton administration policy that took effect Jan. 1 relaxing limits on encryption exports.

To get the export license, Glenwood, Maryland-based Trusted Information Systems had to show the government plans to incorporate so-called key recovery features into future products by the end of 1998.
With key recovery features, the government can decode an encrypted message by recovering the software "key" under a search warrant or similiar authority.
Since the company is already shipping an Internet product including its patented key recovery system, it had few problems meeting the requirement.

The Commerce Department's announcement came just days after a graduate student in California said he had cracked a message encoded with 40-bit encryption, the export limit under the previous policy, in less than four hours.

"Recent attacks on 40-bit encryption have shown that a global move to at least 56-bit (U.S. government standard) security must come soon," Trusted Information executive vice president Steven Lipner said.
In addition to exporting 56-bit products without key recovery, the company said it is also seeking approval to export a 128-bit product with key recovery.
